name: Fatima Alvarez
think: My real worry is **short-time weeks** on 60% pay, not AI.
With about **two weeks saved**, one bad car order hurts every time.
privateAnswer: AI was never my worry. Short-time weeks on 60% pay, with two weeks of money in the bank, are my worry. So nothing changes for me, and that's not the same as fine.

name: Marco Gupta
think: The plateau changes nothing about my **lowest-grade pay** or rising rent.
Corvell depends on **one car maker**, so short weeks are the real threat.
privateAnswer: Honestly, it doesn't fix anything for me. My pay is still the lowest grade, the rent on our flat still goes up every spring, and Corvell still only has one big customer. If that car maker sneezes, we're the ones on short weeks.

name: Uma Nakamura
think: I'm stuck on the **bottom rate** unless I push myself.
With only **two machine shops** in town, I can't move up elsewhere.
privateAnswer: Privately, it means I'm stuck on the bottom rate unless I push myself. The tools I use every day would still help me learn faster than the others. But there's only Halden and one other machine shop in town, so if I don't move up here, I don't move up anywhere.

name: Colin Schmidt
think: I was already worried after Brightwater **lost a contract**.
My rent depends on **overtime** that has dried up.
privateAnswer: Truth is, I was already worried before any of this. Brightwater lost a supermarket contract in the summer and we went off weekend overtime, and overtime is what pays my rent. There's the drinks plant, a warehouse and not much else round here.

name: Dana Ziegler
think: The job's fine, but I'm on the **starter rate** with two weeks saved.
Northfield is the **only food factory** nearby.
privateAnswer: Privately, it's fine for the job, but money's still tight. I'm on the starter rate and I've got about two weeks saved. Northfield is the only food factory round here, so if I mess up there, I'm on a long bus ride to the next one.

name: Karl Fischer
think: Nothing changes for the job, and the **pay stays low** at Kessler.
My **3D printing** sideline is the only thing that grows if I push.
privateAnswer: Privately, nothing changes for the job, and that's the problem, the pay's still low. Kessler is steady enough, but it's the only sheet metal shop in town. My little 3D printing sideline is the only thing that grows if I push it.

name: Sara Mensah
think: Ashby Mill was **struggling** long before anyone mentioned AI.
For me, nothing changing means the **slow squeeze** carries on.
privateAnswer: Privately, Ashby Mill was struggling long before anyone said AI. We lost the big hotel chain to towels from abroad, and they've closed the second weaving shed. For a weaver like me, nothing changing means the slow squeeze on Ashby Mill carries on.

name: Aaron Rossi
think: Boxes always need making, so **Greaves** is fine for now.
Our **money is tight**, under a month saved, with the wedding coming.
privateAnswer: Privately, it's fine for the plant, boxes always need making. But our money's still tight, under a month saved, and the wedding's costing more than we thought. Greaves is the only big employer this side of town.

name: Beth Young
think: I'm **disappointed**, because I liked moving up with the tech.
Hartley's **order book** depends on farmers having good years.
privateAnswer: Privately, I'm a bit disappointed, because I liked the idea of moving up with the tech. Without big change, I'm still on learner pay in a town with three factories. Hartley's order book depends on farmers, and farmers have had a bad couple of years.

name: Ivan Evans
think: I'm relieved my **job stays mine**, but the rent and my warning don't go away.
The small automation lands on **office paperwork**, like Shirin's job, more than on my press.
privateAnswer: Honestly, it means my job stays my job, which is a relief. But my problems don't go anywhere, because the rent's still climbing and my scrap rate is still on a sheet in the office. Nothing in this picture fixes nights or the warning.

name: Priya Larsen
think: Privately, the **lost contract** and four-day weeks still worry me more than any AI.
Nothing changing still leaves Brightpak **one bad order** away from cutting shifts.
privateAnswer: Off the record, Brightpak lost a big supermarket contract last spring, and we went down to four-day weeks for two months. If AI is a flop, the lost supermarket contract and the four-day weeks are still sitting there. Nothing changing isn't the same as everything being fine.

name: Yusuf Rahman
think: Privately, my job looks **steady**, because Kessler has orders and needs code-readers.
With about **four months saved**, I'm not close to the edge.
privateAnswer: Off the record, it's probably fine for me. Kessler has steady orders, and a lathe operator who can actually read the code is worth keeping. My savings are about four months, so I'm not on the edge.

name: Freya Weber
think: Privately, **the new owners** worry me more than AI ever did.
They already **closed a factory** up north and moved the work somewhere cheaper.
privateAnswer: Off the record, I'm relieved, but the new owners still worry me. AI or no AI, the new owners closed a factory up north and moved the work somewhere cheaper. That could happen to us at the biscuit factory.

name: Gareth Diaz
think: Privately, my job **stays my job**, because warehouses keep needing shelving.
With **four months saved** and shared rent, I'm in decent shape.
privateAnswer: Off the record, warehouses keep getting built, so people keep needing shelving. As long as that's true, my job on the stamping press stays my job. I've got about four months saved and I share the flat with Owen, my mate, so the rent's not bad.

name: Nora Khan
think: Privately, nothing changes: drinks sell and the **plant is busy**.
Living alone on manageable rent with **five months saved** feels secure.
privateAnswer: Off the record, nothing really changes for me. The plant is busy, drinks always sell, and I live alone with my cat on a rent I can manage. I've got about five months saved.

name: Victor Petrov
think: Privately, money's tight because **the wedding** is eating the savings.
Window orders drop when **house building slows**, and it has.
privateAnswer: Off the record, I'm relieved, but money's still tight this year. Anna and I are getting married next summer, and the wedding is eating the savings. Window orders also drop when house building slows, and it's been slow.

name: Daria Wagner
think: Privately, the mill's real problem is **cheap imported socks**, not AI.
We went on **short weeks twice** last year when a shop changed suppliers.
privateAnswer: Off the record, we went on short weeks twice last year when a big shop changed suppliers. The mill's real problem is cheap socks from abroad, not AI. That worry doesn't go anywhere just because the robots didn't come.

name: Emeka Chen
think: Privately, **kitchens keep selling**, so the factory is steady.
Four months saved and **bench sales** make me feel secure.
privateAnswer: Off the record, it's good for me. Kitchens keep selling, and the factory isn't going anywhere. I live on my own in a rented flat, I've got about four months saved, and the benches bring in a few hundred a month in summer.

name: Lena Ito
think: Privately, my **steady nights** and decent pay just carry on as they are.
My **nine months** of savings keep growing and the planning office takes whatever AI change there is.
privateAnswer: Honestly, my life stays the way I like it, and the only thing that changes is the planning office gets some software. I've got about nine months of pay saved from the years I lived with my gran, and the shift premium keeps it growing.

name: Tomas Olsen
think: Privately, little changes; the plant still needs **people at the lathes**.
Our real squeeze is **rent** near my girlfriend's school, not technology.
privateAnswer: Privately it means nothing much changes for me. My girlfriend Ines teaches at a primary school, we split the rent, and I've got eight months saved plus a bit my grandad left me in an index fund. The plant still needs people at the lathes.

name: Bianca Usman
think: My plan to move from running the wrapper to **fixing it** still works.
My partner's **bank testing** job stays safe in this picture too.
privateAnswer: For me it means the plan I already have still works. I want to move from running the wrapper to fixing it, so I'm learning PLCs, the little computers that control the line. My partner Kofi tests software for a bank, and his job's safe in this picture too.

name: Carlos Baker
think: Privately, my **press** doesn't care about chatbots, so nothing changes.
I own my flat **outright** from my aunt and have savings on top.
privateAnswer: For me it means nothing. My press doesn't care about chatbots. I own my flat outright, because my aunt left it to me, so I've got no rent, and I've got a fair bit saved on top.

name: Jade Hansen
think: Privately, we stay on track to buy a **small house** in about two years.
My partner's electrician work plus **eight months** saved keeps us steady.
privateAnswer: Privately, it means we stay on track. My partner Sam is an electrician, and we've got about eight months of pay saved, plus a separate house deposit fund. If nothing changes, we buy a small house in about two years.

name: Rafael Novak
think: Privately, nothing changes; I'm the one who keeps the **line fed**.
A bit over a **year of pay** in an index fund means I'm not worried.
privateAnswer: Privately, it changes nothing for me. The line already runs mostly by machine, and I'm the person who keeps it fed. I've got a bit over a year of pay in an index fund, so I'm not worried.

name: Zoe Tanaka
think: Privately, life goes on as planned with **seven months** saved and our house.
We want to start a **family** in the next couple of years.
privateAnswer: For me it means life goes on as planned. My husband Luke repairs farm machinery, we've got about seven months saved, and my parents helped us with the house deposit. We want to start a family in the next couple of years.

name: Adam Abbott
think: My **wedding** plans stay on track with seven months saved.
A share in a **rental flat** with my dad adds a cushion.
privateAnswer: For me it means my plans stay on track. Rosa and I are getting married next summer, and I've got about seven months of pay saved, plus a share in a small rental flat with my dad. The factory needs people, and I'm getting better.

name: Hana Gupta
think: My plan to move from the press to **quality checking** still works.
My **own flat**, small mortgage and eight months saved keep me secure.
privateAnswer: For me it means my plan works as it is. I want to move from the press to quality checking in a couple of years. I've got my own flat with a small mortgage, help from my father on the deposit, and about eight months saved.

name: Omar Moreau
think: I think nothing changes for me, because my problems are **low pay** and thin savings.
I think the real danger is the car maker **moving the contract**, not AI.
privateAnswer: Off the record, it doesn't really fix anything for me. The plant cut the night shift last spring because the car maker ordered less, and that has nothing to do with AI. I'm still on low pay with less than a month saved, so a quiet AI future just means the same tight life.

name: Wendy Schmidt
think: I think it's a relief, but I'm still **one bad month** from asking my mum for money.
I think the **winter shift cuts** are the real danger, not AI.
privateAnswer: Honestly, it's a bit of a relief, but my life's still tight. I'm still on low pay, still one bad month from asking my mum for money. The plant's fine for now, but nothing about AI going quiet fixes the rent.

name: Erik Zhang
think: I think it's **disappointing**, because a shake-up might have forced better training.
I think I'm **stuck** on lower pay with Jun's degree still two years off.
privateAnswer: Off the record, it's a bit disappointing, because I was hoping AI would push our boss to pay for better training. Without a shake-up, I'm stuck on lower pay in a small firm with nowhere else nearby. Jun's degree is two more years, and we're just scraping by.

name: Fatima Fischer
think: I think my **job stays** as it is, which is what I want.
I think my **money** still doesn't get better, so I keep counting every week.
privateAnswer: Honestly, it means my job stays as it is, which is what I want. I'm not interested in computers and I don't use the AI things. But my money doesn't get better either, so I'm still counting every week.

name: Marco Lopez
think: I think my **job doesn't change**, which is fine.
I think fine isn't great on **lower pay** while saving for a flat.
privateAnswer: Honestly, it's fine for me, because my job doesn't change. But fine isn't great when you're on lower pay and trying to buy a flat. I'd still be stuck on the same money.

name: Uma Rossi
think: I think my **job stays**, which is mostly good news.
I think I'd still feel **stuck** on low pay with one plant nearby.
privateAnswer: Honestly, for me it's mostly good news, because my job stays. But my pay doesn't go up, and there's still only one plant like ours nearby. So I'd still feel stuck, just not threatened.

name: Colin Yilmaz
think: I think AI changes **nothing** for me, which is fine.
I think the **shift cut** at the brick works worries me more.
privateAnswer: Honestly, it changes nothing for me, which is fine. But building's slow this year and the works cut a shift in October. That worries me more than any computer.

name: Dana Evans
think: I think my **job stays**, which is what I want.
I think the **winters** are still hard on low pay.
privateAnswer: Honestly, it's fine for me. My job stays and that's what I want. But the winters are still hard, and the pay's still low.

name: Karl Kowalski
think: I think it's **disappointing**, because I hoped to ride the change upward.
I think I'm **stuck** on lower pay with no competing plants nearby.
privateAnswer: Honestly, I'm a bit disappointed, because I was hoping to ride the change to a better job. Without it, I'm stuck on lower pay at a plant with no competition nearby. It's fine, but it's not going anywhere.

name: Sara Rahman
think: I think the **old pressures** stay: rent rising and a plant that already lost a contract.
I'm not safe just because AI fizzles; a **cut shift** still hurts us.
privateAnswer: Honestly, it doesn't make my life easy, it just leaves the old problems. The plant lost the vent cover contract to a cheaper plant last year and nights got cut from five to four for a while. Rent keeps climbing and pay doesn't. The night premium isn't extra money anymore, it's just the rent. So no AI doesn't mean no worry.

name: Aaron Walsh
think: I think my job is **secure**, because the **order book** is full.
I'd mainly gain from **fewer wrong programs** reaching my lathes.
privateAnswer: Honestly it'd suit me. The firm's order book is full with farm machinery parts, so my lathes keep turning whether AI is hype or not. The only thing that changes is maybe fewer wrong programs coming from the office, which is good for me.

name: Beth Diaz
think: I think my job is **steady**, because the plant runs three shifts.
I see **line speed-ups** from management as the real pressure.
privateAnswer: Honestly it'd be fine for me. My job's steady, the plant runs three shifts and frozen pizza isn't going out of fashion. The only pressure is the line speed going up, and that's management, not AI.

name: Ivan Jensen
think: I think nothing changes for me, and that's how I **like it**.
There's a **second press shop** on the estate if this one ever closed.
privateAnswer: For me nothing changes, which is how I like it. The plant's been steady for years, washing machines always break. There's a press shop across the estate too, so if this one closed I'd probably get on there.

name: Priya Petrov
think: I think the plant is **busy** because own-brand drinks sell when money's tight.
My real worry is rebuilding **savings** after the gearbox.
privateAnswer: Honestly it's good for me. Own-brand drinks sell more when money's tight, so the bottling plant stays busy. My only worry is building the savings back up after the gearbox.

name: Yusuf Varga
think: I think the **extrusion work** stays, because people always need windows.
I'm a bit **disappointed** because I wanted to see more.
privateAnswer: Honestly, it changes little for me. The plant is busy, people always need windows, and the extrusion work doesn't go anywhere. I'd be fine.

name: Freya Chen
think: I think **cheap imports** threaten the factory more than AI.
I could be on **short time** again this winter.
privateAnswer: But the honest truth is the factory has its own problems. The imports are cheaper and the big shops buy on price. AI or no AI, I could be on short time again this winter.

name: Gareth Ibrahim
think: My real worry is the **order book**, since one lost car contract means short time.
Office **scheduling software** is fine by me if it stops the rota changing at midnight.
privateAnswer: Off the record, AI was never my worry, the order book is. If Corbett loses another car contract, we go back on short time whether there's AI or not. The office might use it for scheduling, which is fine by me if the rota stops changing at midnight.

name: Nora Olsen
think: Brookfield is **busy**, with summer orders rising, so the plant feels safe.
AI stays useful for **fault codes** and study, which suits me fine.
privateAnswer: For me it'd be fine. I'd keep using the AI tools for what they're good at, which is explaining fault codes and helping me study, and I'd keep moving toward a technician job. Brookfield is busy, summer orders keep going up, and the plant isn't going anywhere.

name: Victor Torres
think: It would be a **relief**, and I'd feel a bit smug about it.
My job lives in my **hands and ears**, so office software doesn't reach me.
The real fight at Kessler stays **pay, shifts and safety**.
privateAnswer: Honestly, it'd be a relief, and I'd feel a bit smug. My job is in my hands and my ears, not on a screen, so some software in the office doesn't touch me. The real fight at Kessler stays what it's always been: pay, shifts and safety.

name: Daria Baker
think: My work is **hands and eyes** in a clean room, untouched by office software.
I'd still have a **decent job** in a town full of plants.
privateAnswer: For me, nothing much changes. My work is hands and eyes in a clean room, and some scheduling software in the office isn't going to load a mould. I'd still have a decent job in a town with plenty of plants.

name: Emeka Haddad
think: I'd be **fine**: well paid, with plants all over this side of town.
My move into **controls work** would just take the normal route.
privateAnswer: Privately, I'd be fine. I'm well paid for an operator, and there are bakeries and packaging plants all over this side of town. It'd just mean my plan to move into controls work takes the normal route, not a fast one.

name: Lena Novak
think: Nothing changes for me, which **suits me** fine.
I'd still be on **nights** on the same stamping line.
privateAnswer: It means nothing changes for me, which suits me. I'd still be on nights, still on the same line. I like my life the way it is.

name: Tomas Silva
think: My job is on the **floor**, and chatbots don't touch it.
A plateau would be **good news** for us.
privateAnswer: For me, honestly, nothing. My job is on the floor, and the floor doesn't care about chatbots. It'd be good news.

name: Bianca Abbott
think: My job is **hands-on**, feeding and fixing already automated machines.
I'd simply **carry on** as before.
The **process technician** promotion would still be my next step.
privateAnswer: For me it's pretty much fine. My job is very hands-on, and the machines are already automated, they just need someone like me to keep them fed and fix them. I'd carry on.

name: Carlos Garcia
think: I'd feel **relieved**, with a good wage, a year saved and plants nearby.
My real worries stay the old ones: **cheaper countries** and my back at forty.
privateAnswer: Off the record, I'd be relieved. I've got a good wage for an operator, a year saved, and plenty of other plants within twenty minutes if mine ever closed. If AI is mostly hype, my biggest worry is still my back at forty, not a computer.

name: Jade Moreau
think: Our plans **hold**, with good pay, plants nearby and steady work for Tomás.
The real pressure would be the **wedding budget** and rising house prices.
privateAnswer: Privately, it just means our plans hold. My job's well paid for what it is, there are three other moulding plants within half an hour, and Tomás always has work. With AI mostly hype, the thing on my mind would be the wedding budget, not the machines.

name: Rafael Santos
think: My job is **safe**, with four other shops in walking distance.
My real project stays the **garage unit** and motorbike parts business.
privateAnswer: Privately it means my job's safe and my plans don't change. Machinists with my pay and experience are always wanted on the estate, there are four other shops within walking distance. If AI stays a fancy calculator, my real project is still the garage unit and the motorbike parts.

name: Zoe Zhang
think: Life stays as **tight** as it is now, with under a month of rent saved.
Another **short-time** spell like last spring would send me back to borrowing from my sister.
privateAnswer: Off the record, it means my life stays exactly as tight as it is now. I've got less than a month of rent saved. Last spring we had three weeks of short-time when the big supermarket order dropped, and I had to borrow from my sister Lin. Nothing changing doesn't mean nothing to worry about.

name: Adam Farah
think: His job is safe with Kessel's **order book** full until 2028.
With **three weeks** saved and covering rent, safe still isn't comfortable.
privateAnswer: Privately, my job's safe in that world, Kessel's order book is full till 2028. But safe and comfortable aren't the same. Leila (my girlfriend) is in nursing school and I'm covering most of the rent, and I've got about three weeks of money in the bank.

name: Hana Lopez
think: She's still the **best line lead** on the lowest wage band.
Rent rose **sixty** this year and she has about two weeks saved.
privateAnswer: For me it means I'm still the best line lead on the lowest wage band, in a town with two factories. My rent went up sixty this year and I've got about two weeks of money in the account. AI saving me ten minutes on a fault doesn't touch my rent.

name: Omar Reyes
think: Same worries as now: **overtime** has been thin since a model moved abroad.
Rent takes most of his pay, with about **three weeks** saved.
privateAnswer: Honestly, for me it means the same worries as now. The overtime's been thin since the washing machine people moved one model abroad, and without Saturdays I'm short. I live on my own, the rent's most of my pay, and I've got maybe three weeks of money put by.

name: Wendy Yilmaz
think: Life stays the same, with **four hundred** saved for the wedding in a year.
Tom's warehouse **cut his hours** in summer, and the car needs tyres.
privateAnswer: Privately, it means my life stays the same, which is fine but not great. Me and Tom (my partner) are saving for a wedding and we've managed four hundred in a year. The car needs tyres and Tom's warehouse cut his hours in the summer.

name: Erik Dubois
think: He's **good but underpaid**, with about two weeks saved.
Maya's **salon income** swings, and Tallis is the only board plant nearby.
privateAnswer: Privately, the problem stays the same: I'm good at this and I'm paid like I'm not. I've got about two weeks of money saved, Maya (my girlfriend) rents a chair at a hair salon and her money goes up and down, and Tallis is the only board plant for eighty kilometres.

name: Fatima Kowalski
think: Things stay **hard but honest**, with under a month saved.
Golden Crust keeps talking about cutting the **night premium**.
privateAnswer: Privately, it means things stay hard but honest. I have less than a month of money saved, and Piotr (my fiancé), who's an electrician's apprentice, and I are saving for the wedding in June. The night premium is what makes the money work, and Golden Crust keeps talking about cutting it.

name: Marco Quinn
think: His worries stay the same: **low pay** for both him and Rosa.
When Ashby is **quiet**, overtime goes first, costing about two hundred.
privateAnswer: Truthfully, my worries are the same as now. Rosa (my girlfriend) is a teaching assistant and neither of us earns much. We've got about three weeks saved and the rent went up again. Ashby's had two quiet months this year, and when it's quiet, the overtime goes first.

name: Uma Walsh
think: The **filling** job looks steady, but low pay and less than one month saved keep me alert.
**Few** nearby factory jobs make a missed wage hard to replace.
privateAnswer: I expect the filling line to keep running, yet my low wage leaves little room if a shift is cancelled. With less than a month saved and few other factories nearby, even the ordinary bills make me careful.

name: Colin Costa
think: The real threat on our floor is the **robot arm** on Press 4, not AI.
A stalled AI doesn't stop the company buying **more arms** that each cost a job.
privateAnswer: Privately, I'd still be watching that robot arm on Press 4. Plateau or not, the company put it in last spring to take parts out of the mould, and it cost us one job on each shift. AI stalling doesn't stop them buying more arms like that one.

name: Dana Jensen
think: AI would only save me about **twenty minutes** a shift on rota and notes.
The **machines and crew** are the real job, and that stays the same.
privateAnswer: Privately, I'd be pretty settled. The bits AI would save me are the rota and the handover notes, which is maybe twenty minutes a shift. The machines and the crew are the job, and that doesn't change.

name: Karl Patel
think: The chatbot still catches **code mistakes**, and the shop still needs me.
I'd only have been **too excited**, nothing worse.
privateAnswer: Privately, I'd be fine. The chatbot would still catch my code mistakes, and the machines still need someone like me. It'd just mean I'd been a bit too excited.

name: Sara Varga
think: AI stalling doesn't fix our real problem: **falling box orders**, down about 15%.
Losing **Saturday overtime** already cut my pay.
privateAnswer: Privately, AI going nowhere doesn't fix our real problem. Box orders are down about 15% this year because online shops are using less packaging. Management already cut Saturday overtime, and that was a good chunk of my pay.

name: Aaron Bauer
think: Kessler's **order book** is decent and my skills are valued.
My one real annoyance is **house prices**, which AI doesn't change.
privateAnswer: Privately, I'd be pleased. Kessler's order book is decent, and I'm the fastest on die changes. My press job was never going anywhere. The only thing that annoys me is house prices, and AI doesn't change those.

name: Beth Ibrahim
think: Corvan is **growing** and medicines always need making.
The **twenty minutes** saved on paperwork is a bonus, not a threat.
privateAnswer: Privately, I'd be fine. Corvan's growing. Medicines always need making, and I'm good at what I do. The twenty minutes of paperwork I've saved is a nice bonus, not a threat.

name: Ivan Okafor
think: I'd be **glad**, as I don't use AI and would rather not.
Hollins is **busy** and I run the line, so I'm settled.
privateAnswer: Privately, I'd be glad. I don't use any of these AI programs and I'd rather not start. Hollins is busy with kitchen orders and I'm the one who runs the line, so I'm settled.

name: Priya Torres
think: Ashby has **steady orders** and I'm senior on my shift.
The one thing I watch is car makers **moving orders abroad**.
privateAnswer: Privately, I'd be relieved. Ashby has steady orders from the car industry, and I'm the senior on my shift. The only thing I watch is whether the car makers keep buying from us or go abroad.

name: Yusuf Alvarez
think: **Regular** shifts and typical pay cover current bills.
A **few** months saved and some nearby plants give me time if this one fails.
privateAnswer: I can keep earning the ordinary operator wage in this picture. My savings would cover a few months if shifts stopped, and some other plants are close enough to approach; neither is a reason to waste a good job.

name: Freya Haddad
think: My **senior wage** is secure under modest software change.
Ten months of **savings** and many nearby plants give me room, even with rent.
privateAnswer: My senior rate is good, and I have ten months of expenses saved from years of weekend shifts. Similar factories are hiring nearby. A quiet change leaves my wage secure, though I still pay rent on my flat.

name: Gareth Nakamura
think: Our **lead wage** and the bakery income continue in the mild case.
Nine months of **savings** give us a strong base for a flat.
privateAnswer: I earn a higher lead rate, and my partner and I have about nine months of expenses saved. Nearby mills advertise similar work. If the change stays small, our paid shifts and the flat we're saving for still look manageable.

name: Nora Silva
think: Steady **packaging orders** and higher pay make my job secure in this picture.
Our **strong cushion** and nearby plants give Hana and me room to choose.
privateAnswer: Our packaging orders are steady, and I earn more than most operators because I can reset three presses. I live with my partner Hana, have over six months saved, and could find similar factory work nearby if the plant slows.

name: Victor Ziegler
think: Regular **box orders** and the lead rate make my present job secure.
The **rented flat**, savings and nearby plants protect Ines and me against an ordinary gap.
privateAnswer: Our plant has regular orders, I earn the lead rate, and I own a small flat that I let out. My partner Ines and I have more than six months saved, and there are other box plants within reach.

name: Daria Garcia
think: My **higher rate** and savings protect us from a short quiet week.
A copied **batch code** can hide inside a polished form.
privateAnswer: My line hours and higher rate look safe in this mild picture, and the savings can absorb a quiet week. I only worry that a copied batch number could pass through a neat form unnoticed.

name: Emeka Mensah
think: My **operator pay** looks safe in a modest change.
Savings and nearby **plants** give me room to try useful tools.
privateAnswer: My cell has orders and the work stays mostly physical, so I expect my pay to hold. Savings and nearby plants give me room to test useful tools without making every software update a career decision.

name: Lena Santos
think: Regular **bracket orders** and higher pay make my job feel secure.
Our **savings** and nearby factories give Mateo and me options.
privateAnswer: The bracket orders are regular and I am paid well to lead the press setup. My fiancé Mateo and I have more than six months saved, and other metal factories nearby could take an experienced operator if this one slowed.

name: Tomas Young
